name: Audi UI
tagline: Premium-automotive design language spanning web, configurator, and in-car.
origin: Audi UI has roots in the Audi Corporate Identity programs and has matured into a system covering Audi.com, the vehicle configurator, the myAudi customer portal, and the in-vehicle MMI surfaces. The current public guidance is part of the broader Audi CI portal and represents one of the few automotive design systems with serious public documentation.
governance: Audi's central brand and digital design teams maintain the system; component implementations are internal and shared with agency partners under license. Updates ride the longer cadence of automotive product cycles, not SaaS release rhythms.
knownFor: Premium-restraint visual language — wide negative space, monochrome with red accent, type as architecture.
Vehicle configurator patterns — option pickers, conflict resolution between trims, and price breakdown surfaces — are unusually rigorous.
Cross-surface coherence between marketing web, transactional flows (build & price), and in-car HMI.
underrated: The AudiType typeface family is a load-bearing brand asset with weight ramps tuned for both editorial spreads and dense data tables.
The system's accessibility guidance addresses in-vehicle constraints (driver attention, glance time) that pure-web design systems never confront.
watchOutsFor: Patterns assume luxury-automotive context — long consideration cycles, high price points, premium photography. They don't translate to mass-market commerce.
Public guidance is presentational; the production component code is not open. Adopting Audi UI means rebuilding to spec.
evaluationGuidance: Study Audi UI if you're working in automotive, premium goods, or any product whose entire job is communicating restraint and quality. Don't apply it to dense SaaS tools — its patterns assume editorial breathing room.
